pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Fasten and adjust your own seat belt and ask passengers to buckle up before driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Rhode Island's primary seat-belt law allows a traffic stop when someone in the vehicle is unbuckled.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The driver must ensure that adult occupants in any seat use the required safety-belt or shoulder-harness system.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The vehicle operator must also wear the required restraint while driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook lists a forty-dollar safety-belt fine for each unrestrained occupant.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child younger than eight who is also shorter than fifty-seven inches and weighs less than eighty pounds must use an approved child restraint in a rear seat.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For a child younger than eight who has reached either fifty-seven inches or eighty pounds, the handbook permits the required safety belt or shoulder harness in a rear seat.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Passengers from age eight until their eighteenth birthday must use the required safety belt or shoulder harness wherever they sit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Drivers below eighteen must wear the required safety belt or shoulder harness.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The rear-seat requirement for a child younger than eight has exceptions when the vehicle has no rear seat or other children occupy every rear position.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When the rear-seat exception applies and a passenger airbag is present, the oldest child should use the front seat.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A violation involving transport of a child without the required child restraint requires a court appearance.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The child-restraint table says a child still below two years and below thirty pounds must remain in a rear-facing seat.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook recommends keeping a child rear-facing as long as possible and reserves a forward-facing convertible seat for a child who has reached two years.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The lap belt should rest over the hip bones and upper thighs, with the shoulder belt crossing the middle of the chest.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A booster-seat fit check asks whether the child's lower back reaches the vehicle seat and the knees bend at the seat edge.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The fit check also requires the shoulder belt to cross the collarbone and chest center and the lap belt to lie over the hip bones and upper thighs.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child must be able to maintain the proper belt-fitting posture throughout the journey to pass the seat-belt fit check.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Failure of any part of the belt-fit check means the child needs a booster seat for safe travel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A booster seat must be paired with a system that provides both a lap belt and a shoulder belt.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook identifies the rear seat as the safer location for a child's protection from airbags.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stopping requires noticing danger, deciding to respond and operating the brake.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Perception distance is the distance traveled while recognizing the hazard and the need to react.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reaction distance is the distance traveled while moving to apply the brake.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Braking distance measures travel from the application of the brakes until the vehicle stops.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Total stopping distance combines the perception, reaction and braking distances.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook uses approximately three-quarters of a second as the average driver's time to apply the brake after seeing danger.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At higher speeds, the vehicle covers more ground before the brakes can be applied.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wet or icy pavement reduces traction and lengthens braking distance, so the driver must slow down.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Roads can be especially slippery at the start of rain as water mixes with oil, rubber and dirt.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Velocitizing means feeling that the vehicle is moving more slowly than its actual speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After highway travel, take particular care to reduce speed when entering an exit ramp.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Hydroplaning occurs when the front tires lose contact with a wet road and steering control is lost.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reduce hydroplaning risk by slowing down in rain, keeping tire pressure at the manufacturer's recommendation and avoiding pooled water.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before a left turn, signal early enough to warn following traffic and slow gradually while checking the mirror.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Check that a following vehicle is not trying to pass on the left before beginning a left turn.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not cut suddenly across from a right-hand lane to make a left turn; continue to another intersection if proper positioning is no longer possible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep the wheels unturned while waiting for a safe gap before a left turn.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When preparing a left turn, yield to directly approaching traffic and to traffic approaching from the right.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Drivers turning left must yield to pedestrians already in the street.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After completing a turn, cancel the turn signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Begin a right turn from the far-right side of the roadway after giving adequate warning with the turn signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not swing left before a right turn because a following driver may mistake it for a left-turn intention.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wait for the way to clear before turning right, yielding to approaching traffic and pedestrians in the street.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Plan a turn's path and reduce speed before entering the turn.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Through the early part of a turn, remain ready to brake, then accelerate out at a comfortable safe rate.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A turnabout changes the vehicle's direction so it can travel back the other way.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before a turnabout, check for prohibiting signs and local restrictions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook's turnabout checklist requires five hundred feet of visibility in each direction and at least two hundred feet of separation from an intersection.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not choose a turnabout location where hills or curves block the view, space is inadequate, traffic is heavy or pedestrians are in the path.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A U-turn is allowed only where permitted and where it will not interfere with traffic moving in either direction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before a U-turn, signal to move to the right curb, stop and check traffic both ways before starting the turn.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Signal the U-turn intention with the left turn signal or hazard lights and cancel the signal after finishing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Backing into a side street or driveway on the right allows the driver to rejoin the main road by moving forward.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before backing into a driveway on the right, pass the entrance, signal and check for people and traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After backing clear of the curb line into the driveway, stop, check traffic and signal before driving forward onto the main road.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Pulling into a driveway on the left is a more hazardous turnabout because re-entry involves backing into a traffic lane.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For a left-driveway turnabout, stop after clearing the curb line and check for pedestrians and vehicles before reversing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: During the reverse portion of a left-driveway turnabout, steer right and begin straightening around the middle of the turn.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Where permitted, a three-point turn can reverse direction on a narrow street.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Start a three-point turn by choosing a safe place, pulling to the right and stopping with the proper signals.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For the first movement of a three-point turn, check both directions, steer fully left and stop before the opposite curb.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For the second movement, check again, steer fully right and reverse until the vehicle's front reaches about the street's middle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For the final movement, check traffic again, steer left and proceed in the new direction, then cancel the signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wait for approaching vehicles and keep watching pedestrians throughout a turnabout.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook advises a complete stop lasting at least three seconds so that the driver can scan left, right, center and left again.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At a stop sign, stop before the near-side crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, use the marked stop line.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If neither a crosswalk nor stop line exists, stop before entering the intersection at the nearest point that gives a view of approaching traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A police officer or traffic signal directing the vehicle to proceed is an exception to the quoted stop-sign instruction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At a four-way stop, yield to vehicles that completed their stop before you arrived.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When vehicles reach a four-way stop together, yield to the vehicle on your right.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before entering a parking space, use the nearest traffic lane and signal the parking intention.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Once parked, switch off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key and apply the parking brake.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before leaving a parking space, check mirrors and look over the left shoulder for blind-spot traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Signal before leaving a parked position and enter the traffic lane nearest the parking space.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not stop or park on a highway's traveled portion, a sidewalk, an intersection, a bridge, a tunnel or railroad tracks.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Double parking and parking beside roadwork in a way that blocks traffic are prohibited.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not park in front of a driveway, at an accessible curb ramp or wherever a stopping or parking prohibition is posted.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep parked vehicles at least eight feet from a fire hydrant.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not park within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook prohibits parking within thirty feet of a flashing red or yellow light, stop sign or traffic signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not park within twenty feet of a fire-station driveway or, where signed, within seventy-five feet of it on the opposite side.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Parking within fifty feet of the closest rail at a railroad crossing is prohibited except for a brief passenger or package loading or unloading stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a two-lane road, park with the right wheels no farther than twelve inches from the right edge or curb unless parking is prohibited.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a one-way road, either side may be used where lawful, with the vehicle facing traffic's direction and the wheels within twelve inches of the edge.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a hill, the parking brake must keep a stopped vehicle from rolling backward.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before starting uphill from the curb, check over the left shoulder, select the gear, signal and release the parking brake before carefully moving out.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before a lane change, confirm the lane is available, signal in time and check mirrors and the shoulder blind spot.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When emerging from a driveway, stop at the sidewalk to check pedestrians and then stop again at the curb to check roadway traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before overtaking, confirm that the pass is lawful, safe and worthwhile.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The turnabout checklist says not to cross a solid yellow line while making a turnabout.
